etymologies.heading: Etymology
paragraphs: From Serendip (“variant of Serendib: Ceylon, Sri Lanka”) +‎ -ity. Coined by English writer and politician Horace Walpole in 1754 based on the Persian story of the Three Princes of Serendip, who (Walpole wrote to a friend) were “always making discoveries, by accidents and sagacity, of things which they were not in quest of”.
senses: The phenomenon of making an unplanned, fortunate discovery through a combination of unexpected circumstances and insightful recognition.
An unsought, unintended or unexpected, but fortunate, discovery or learning experience that occurs by accident.
